blocks.name: AES-GCM core
blocks.summary: AES-GCM authenticated encryption and decryption (FIPS 197, NIST SP 800-38D, CCSDS 352.0-B-2) with a key table, IV generation per key slot and a register file; one message per context, one status per message.
notes: Rst is synchronous and high-active; synchronise its release to Clk, for example with olo_base_reset_gen with SyncTmr_g = true.
After the reset the key table erases every slot (NumKeys_g cycles, STATUS.BUSY = '1'); no key survives a reset.
One context per message, in the order of the messages; the core pairs the n-th context with the n-th message.
Load every key slot in use through the registers before sending contexts (programming sequence of the user guide).
Without the release buffer, discard every decrypted message whose last beat carries the error flag or whose status is not OK.
Save the invocation counter of every slot with generated IVs regularly ahead of the operational value (GCM 9.1).

rules.message: Set DenseOutput_g = true, so that every message leaves as one gapless byte string (IV, AAD, ciphertext, tag); the sectioned output is for the input of a second core (decryption).

The error flag of the messages (user bit 2 on the last beat) is not passed on, so a message that failed (for example with KEY) is sent like a good one. Set ReleaseBuffer_g = true (a message leaves the core only when its status is OK) with ReleaseBytes_g of at least the longest message, or consume the status at M_Sts.

init.text: After the reset wait until STATUS (0x014) bit 0 BUSY is 0: the key table erases every slot.

Load every key slot in use: write the key to KEY0 to KEY7 (0x040 + 4 n; key byte 4 n in bits 31:24; 4, 6 or 8 words), for generated IVs the fixed field to IV_FIXED (0x060) and the first invocation counter to IV_COUNT_LO (0x064) and IV_COUNT_HI (0x068), then write KEY_LOAD (0x06C) with START (bit 31), IV_GEN (bit 8) and the slot (bits 7:0), for example 0x80000100 for slot 0 with generated IVs; wait until STATUS.BUSY is 0.

blocks.endToEnd: Load the key slot, send a packet and check the output: with generated IVs the first 4 bytes of every message are IV_FIXED, the next 8 the invocation counter; decrypt it with AES-GCM in the test bench (or a second core) and compare.

blocks.name: Chunk framer
blocks.summary: Cuts packets of any length into chunks of ChunkBytes_g bytes and hands every chunk to the AES-GCM core as one encryption with a generated IV and a 4-byte AAD with the position of the chunk in its packet.
notes: The slot Cfg_Slot is loaded for generated IVs and stays unchanged while the framer holds chunks.
Every chunk consumes one invocation of the slot; save the counter regularly (GCM 9.1).
A receiver decrypts every chunk on its own (IV bytes 0 to 11, AAD bytes 12 to 15, tag the last 16 bytes), orders the chunks by the invocation counter and finds the packet boundaries in the positions.

rules.message: The framer and the core share clock and reset; a reset of only one of them leaves contexts or messages without partner.

init.text: Load the key slot Cfg_Slot of the AES-GCM core for generated IVs (KEY_LOAD with IV_GEN = '1', see the core) before the first packet; without a loaded slot every chunk fails with KEY.

blocks.name: SpaceFibre port
blocks.summary: SpaceFibre node interface of one port according to ECSS-E-ST-50-11C: virtual channels and broadcast messages, Data Link, Multi-Lane and Lane layers and the Management Information Base, for 1 to 4 lanes. The physical adapter (transceivers) is a separate block.
notes: The VC ports have the link format of OpenSPP: spp_core with DataWidth_g = 32 x NumLanes_g connects to a VC port directly (M_Link_User(0) to S_Vc_TUser); the further user bits of OpenSPP (destination index) do not reach the SpaceFibre port.
Every VC carries any packets; which VC carries which traffic is a convention of the system that both ends of the link follow.
Enable the safe implementation of state machines in the synthesis tool (Vivado FSM_SAFE_STATE = default_state on the state registers, Synplify syn_encoding = safe).

Read ID (0x0FB10007) and GENERICS after the reset; start the link with LANE_CTRL = 0x63 at one end (LaneStart, AutoStart, TxEn, RxEn) and wait for DL_STATUS bits 1:0 = 3 (programming sequence of the user guide).
All four clocks must run for the reset to complete; CoreClk may be the lane clock (as in the VCK190 reference design).

rules.message: CoreClk must run at least as fast as LaneClk; a slower CoreClk loses received rows (DL_ERRORS bit 10).
UserClk slower than LaneClk limits the throughput of the virtual channels (one beat of NumLanes_g words per cycle).

ofb_core leaves reset before the transceivers are ready: the lane initialisation can start against a transmitter that is still in reset, and the Composer cannot couple LaneRst of the adapter to the reset of the core yet.

constraints.note: Clock crossings inside the core (Open Logic): for every pair of its clocks, in both directions, the period of the faster clock.

init.text: Start the link at one end: write LANE_CTRL (0x100 + 0x20 i) of every lane i = 0x63 (LaneStart, AutoStart, TxEn, RxEn); the reset value 0x62 (AutoStart) starts when the far end sends.
Wait for LANE_STATUS (0x104 + 0x20 i) bits 3:0 = 7 (Active) of the lanes and DL_STATUS (0x010) bits 1:0 = 3 (link initialised); VC_HAS_CREDIT (0x030) shows the VCs that may send.

blocks.endToEnd: Connect two nodes (in a simulation without the transceiver models: two cores joined by tb/ofb_tb_pa_model.vhd of OpenFibre), start the link at one end and send a packet on a virtual channel; it arrives on the same virtual channel at the other end.

blocks.summary: Physical adapter of OpenFibre for one AMD Versal GTY quad (vendor-specific): 8B/10B, comma alignment and receive clock correction in the transceivers at 6.25 Gbit/s. Its lane clock output is the lane clock of the core.
notes: Vendor-specific (AMD Versal GTY). hdl/ofb_pa_gty/src/ofb_pa_gty.vhd is not in component_list.txt: add it to the library openfibre, and create the transceiver wizard instance ofb_gtw in the Vivado project with hdl/ofb_pa_gty/tcl/ofb_gtw.tcl (source the file, then ofb_gtw_create ofb_gtw 156.25 for a 156.25 MHz reference clock).
RefClk is the output O of the IBUFDS_GTE5 of the reference clock pins of the quad; place the buffer in the chip-level top, as hdl/ofb_vck190/src/ofb_vck190_top.vhd does.
Hold the reset of the core while LaneRst is high; the VCK190 reference design synchronises LaneRst to MgmtClk and ORs it with the power-on reset into Rst of the core.
The line rate is 6.25 Gbit/s with a 156.25 MHz reference clock, so LaneClk runs at 156.25 MHz.

Simulation needs the AMD transceiver models (unisim and the simulation files of the wizard); OpenFibre simulates the adapter with tools/run_xsim.py. Without them, the test bench model tb/ofb_tb_pa_model.vhd of OpenFibre (two adapters joined by a lane, one clock) stands in for the adapters of both ends of a link.

blocks.name: RMAP node
blocks.summary: RMAP target and initiator according to ECSS-E-ST-50-52C on SpaceWire packet ports, with a memory master, a pass-through port for other protocols and a register file.
notes: Rst is synchronous and high-active; synchronise its release to Clk, for example with olo_base_reset_gen.
M_RepData, M_Conf and M_User must be served when connected; a stalled output stalls the received packet stream and the link.
RMAP address bits above AxiAddrWidth_g must be zero in the windows.

With AxiMaxBeats_g = 1 and AxiDataWidth_g = 32 the memory master issues single transfers only and can drive an AXI4-Lite slave; tie M_Axi_RLast to '1'. Known defect of the pinned version (fix in progress in OpenRMAP): with AxiMaxBeats_g < 4, commands longer than one AXI transaction return or write wrong data.

rules.message: At least one of Target_g and Initiator_g must be true.
Two nodes that are initiator and target of each other on one link need Transactions_g = 1.
The RMAP node normally runs on the user clock of its SpaceWire port; an asynchronous FIFO was inserted instead.
Known defect: commands longer than one AXI transaction return or write wrong data with AxiMaxBeats_g < 4; fix in progress in OpenRMAP.

init.text: None needed: with the default generics the target accepts every command to the logical address 0xFE with the key 0x00 on the whole address space (WinInit_g). A flight configuration narrows the logical addresses (TGT_LA 0x010), the key (TGT_KEY) and the windows (WIN_BASE, WIN_LAST, WIN_CTRL), see the register map.

blocks.name: Space Packet node
blocks.summary: Space Packet Protocol (CCSDS 133.0-B-2) with the CPTP layer of ECSS-E-ST-50-53C: send and receive ports with Octet String or Packet Service, APID routing and a register file.
notes: Rst is synchronous and high-active; synchronise its release to Clk, for example with olo_base_reset_gen.
After the reset the core initialises both APID tables (2048 clock cycles); packets are sent and delivered once the tables are ready.
Serve every receive port, or place a buffer behind a port whose user can stall for long.
TxBufferBytes_g holds the longest SDU of a port, RxBufferBytes_g the longest Space Packet.
Hold the side band (TUser) of a send port constant during an SDU.
A last beat without valid bytes (Keep all zero) ends an SDU or packet at the inputs; an SDU without any byte is rejected (0x02). The outputs never carry a beat without valid bytes.
The user supplies the packet secondary header at the start of the Octet String and keeps the secondary header flag of an APID static.

init.text: After the reset wait until TABLE_STATUS (0x040) bits 1:0 (TX_BUSY, RX_BUSY) are 0: the core initialises both APID tables (2048 clock cycles).

Nothing else is needed: with TxPathDefault_g and RxPathDefault_g every APID has an enabled path to destination 0 and to receive port 0, destination 0 has the Target Logical Address 0xFE (DEST_CTRL 0x400) and the own address is Tla_g. A flight configuration writes the APID tables (TX_TABLE_APID 0x030 and TX_TABLE_ENTRY 0x034, RX_TABLE_APID 0x038 and RX_TABLE_ENTRY 0x03C) and the destinations (DEST_CTRL 0x400 + 0x20 n).

Enable the managed data paths: for every APID write TX_TABLE_APID (0x030), read TX_TABLE_ENTRY (0x034), write it with ENABLE and DEST, read it again; the same with RX_TABLE_APID (0x038) and RX_TABLE_ENTRY (0x03C) with ENABLE and PORT; write the destinations (DEST_CTRL 0x400 + 0x20 n).

blocks.endToEnd: Send one SDU on a send port (APID 0x123, for example) and expect it on receive port 0 with the same APID in user bits 10:0, once the APID tables are ready.

blocks.name: SpaceWire port
blocks.summary: SpaceWire port according to ECSS-E-ST-50-12C Rev.1: encoding, data link and network services (packets, time-codes, distributed interrupts) with a register file.
notes: LVDS output buffers for data and strobe and LVDS input buffers with fail-safe biasing belong to the top level; the core contains no I/O buffer.
Enable the safe implementation of state machines in the synthesis tool.
Set INT_HOLDOFF and INT_ACK_DELAY for the network before distributed interrupts are used.
Serve the indication ports before the indication FIFO (16 entries) fills.
Write registers as 32-bit words; a read that depends on a write waits for the write response.

rules.message: A receiver samples a bit period that is longer than 1.2 of its LinkClk periods (user guide, section 3)

constraints.note: Clock crossings inside the core (Open Logic FT FIFOs and synchronisers): for every pair of its clocks, in both directions, the period of the faster clock; no asynchronous clock groups.
Place the output flip-flops of data and strobe in the I/O blocks with matched routing.

init.text: Optionally write LINK_SPEED (0x14) bits 7:0 RUN_DIV: the bit period in the Run state in LinkClk cycles (reset value RunDiv_g); choose it for the far end, which samples at most about LinkClk / 1.2.
Write PORT_CTRL (0x10) = 0x34 (RECEIVER_EN, DRIVER_EN, LINK_START) to start the link, or 0x38 (AUTO_START) to wait for the far end.
The link starts after the reset without software (LinkStart_g or AutoStart_g).
The link starts after the reset without software (LinkStart_g or AutoStart_g).
Wait for PORT_STATUS (0x18) bits 2:0 LINK_STATE = 5 (Run) before packets are exchanged.

blocks.endToEnd: Loop the SpaceWire line back (Spw_DOut to Spw_DIn, Spw_SOut to Spw_SIn) or connect a second port, start the link and wait for PORT_STATUS LINK_STATE = 5 (Run).
